title: Survival Model Evaluation
interviewAnswer: Survival models require metrics that handle censoring, such as concordance index and time-dependent calibration/Brier scores. Ordinary classification metrics at arbitrary cutoffs can discard useful time information.
why: Survival Model Evaluation appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: Survival models require metrics that handle censoring, such as concordance index and time-dependent calibration/Brier scores. Ordinary classification metrics at arbitrary cutoffs can discard useful time information. Calibration matters at relevant horizons. Evaluation must account for censoring. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Evaluate whether higher predicted risk corresponds to earlier churn and whether 90-day survival probabilities are calibrated.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Survival Model Evaluation make?
How would you validate or debug Survival Model Evaluation in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
